en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and is endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous ancestors over 2,000 years ago for agriculture.
The Supreme Court is the highest court in the Philippines and leads the judicial branch of the government.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first female student admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator for babies.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Tboli people of South Cotabato weave the Tnalak, a traditional cloth made from abaca fibers dyed with natural plants.
The Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo, Aklan, honors the Santo Niño with participants painting their faces and dancing in the streets.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his masterpiece Spoliarium.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system where characters represent syllables, and it was written on bamboo and leaves.
Julian Felipe composed the music for the Philippine national anthem, Lupang Hinirang, in 1898 to celebrate the declaration of independence.
Gregorio Zara, a Filipino scientist, invented the two-way television telephone and discovered the physical phenomenon now called the Zara effect.
